scope: D3D8 additional backbuffer public COM counts are independent of private texture references. The chain owns the storage creation device pin; a live public surface owns one additional device/storage pin only across public count 0-to-1 / 1-to-0 edges. Zero-count cached views and stores survive while a chain or target binding keeps storage alive. Validate repeated zero Release, direct/cached revival, last-view device destruction, and successful Reset when storage is held only by a device binding. Ordinary texture forwarding and implicit surface behavior are retained. D3D8 additional-chain physical lifetime/revival while its public chain count is zero, D3D9 chain containers/independent surface counters, multiple buffers, standalone render/depth counters, complete Reset, original Microsoft HAL, games/FPS and review stages 4/5/6 remain incomplete. No host/protocol/shader change or new GPU pixel run; inherit the rebuilt 7a baseline.

sources.evidence: Pinned Windows additional-chain reference test: creating the chain adds one device reference; getting the backbuffer returns public count 1 and adds one device pin; subsequent AddRef preserves device count, final public Release returns zero, cached AddRef at zero is valid while chain survives and repeated zero Release returns zero.

Surface AddRef/Release maintain their own resource.refcount for non-texture public surfaces; device and underlying texture/swapchain references change only on public zero/nonzero edges. Release storage before the parent device, since storage destruction can free the surface.
